query: What signals suggest an incident will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Category of the issue is known at open time and plausibly correlates with how long resolution takes (e.g., database vs email). Legitimate predictor outside the focus.

per_column.name: problem_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom type (outage vs cannot_connect) is knowable at intake and carries signal about complexity and time to resolve. Valid predictor.

per_column.name: is_unassigned_at_open
per_column.rationale: Whether an incident lacks an assignee at open time is knowable early and plausibly delays resolution. Legitimate predictor, no leakage.

per_column.name: assignee_resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Whether the assignee matches the resolver requires knowing who ultimately resolved/closed the incident, which is only determined after the outcome. This is post-hoc information correlated with the resolution process itself, constituting leakage.

per_column.name: opened_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Business vs off hours at open time is known before resolution and can affect response latency. Valid predictor derived from opened_at.

per_column.name: is_recurring_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Whether the issue type is recurring is knowable at intake (from category/symptom patterns) and plausibly relates to quicker resolution via known fixes. Legitimate predictor, though heavily skewed (462/38) so limited discriminative power.

judge.rationale: Five of six columns are legitimate, intake-time predictors that plausibly carry signal about resolution_time (category, symptom, unassigned-at-open, opened-hour, recurring-type), giving a model meaningful leverage beyond the raw fields. assignee_resolver_match is leakage because it depends on the eventual resolver/closer, information only available after the outcome. Some predictors are highly skewed, capping the incremental predictive leverage of the set.
